Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates a reticulo-nodular pattern with prominent bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and perihilar opacities, which is the classic radiographic presentation of sarcoidosis (Stage II). This distribution distinguishes it from pneumoconiosis/silicosis (typically upper lobe nodules without significant adenopathy) and pulmonary fibrosis (basal predominance with honeycombing).
